probability.label: Probability
probability.when: to say how likely something is

phrases.connector: …, given that …, and this strongly suggests …
…, and the evidence for this is …
…, which points to …, and as a result …

phrases.t: It is reasonable to expect that …
phrases.connector: …, given the fact that …, and therefore …

tasks.question: How likely is it that most people will work from home in the future?

cues.cue: remote work / become / the norm
models: It is highly likely that remote work will become the norm, given that companies have already adapted their systems, and this strongly suggests offices will shrink in size.

cues.cue: hybrid arrangements / remain / the most common setup
models: In all probability, hybrid arrangements will remain the most common setup, which means that full-time remote work may stay less widespread than expected, and therefore offices will not disappear entirely.

cues.cue: some industries / continue / to require on-site work
models: The chances are that some industries will continue to require on-site work, especially since manual and hands-on jobs cannot be done remotely, so remote work will never be universal.

cues.cue: employees / demand / more flexibility from employers
models: It is almost certain that employees will demand more flexibility from employers, and the evidence for this is the strong preference workers have shown since the shift to remote work began.

cues.cue: technology / make / remote collaboration even easier
models: More likely than not, technology will make remote collaboration even easier, which points to fewer barriers for distributed teams, and as a result remote work will keep expanding.

cues.cue: companies / save / on office costs by going remote
models: One can safely predict that more companies will save on office costs by going remote, since the trend clearly shows businesses already downsizing their premises.

tasks.question: How likely are we to solve the problem of pollution in cities?

cues.cue: pollution / stay / a problem
models: It seems probable that pollution will stay a problem, judging by how slowly regulations are being enforced, and this implies real change will take years.

cues.cue: electric vehicles / help / reduce emissions gradually
models: It is reasonable to expect that electric vehicles will help reduce emissions gradually, given the fact that adoption rates are rising steadily, and therefore air quality should slowly improve.

cues.cue: governments / introduce / stricter environmental laws
models: There is every likelihood that governments will introduce stricter environmental laws, and this is supported by growing public pressure for climate action.

cues.cue: some cities / achieve / cleaner air within a decade
models: It is highly likely that some cities will achieve cleaner air within a decade, given that many have already set ambitious targets, and this strongly suggests measurable progress is possible.

cues.cue: full elimination of pollution / remain / unlikely soon
models: The odds are that full elimination of pollution will remain unlikely soon, which would explain why experts focus on gradual reduction, and so realistic targets matter most.

cues.cue: public transport investment / cut / emissions significantly
models: In all probability, investment in public transport will cut emissions significantly, which means fewer cars on the road, and therefore cities should see steady improvement.

tasks.question: How likely is it that electric cars will replace petrol cars?

cues.cue: electric cars / replace / petrol cars
models: In all probability, electric cars will replace petrol cars, which means that fuel stations will gradually disappear, and therefore infrastructure will need to change dramatically.

cues.cue: battery technology / improve / driving range significantly
models: It is highly likely that battery technology will improve driving range significantly, given that research investment keeps growing, and this strongly suggests remaining concerns will fade.

cues.cue: charging infrastructure / expand / across most countries
models: It is reasonable to expect that charging infrastructure will expand across most countries, given the fact that demand is rising quickly, and therefore range anxiety should ease.

cues.cue: petrol cars / disappear / entirely within decades
models: It seems probable that petrol cars will disappear entirely within decades, judging by current government bans on new sales, and this implies the transition is well underway.

cues.cue: second-hand petrol cars / remain / on roads for years
models: More likely than not, second-hand petrol cars will remain on roads for years, which points to a slower transition than headlines suggest, and as a result full replacement will take time.

cues.cue: prices / fall / making electric cars more accessible
models: One can safely predict that prices will fall, making electric cars more accessible, since the trend clearly shows costs dropping as production scales up.

tasks.question: How likely is it that young people will keep moving to cities?

cues.cue: cities / keep / growing
models: The chances are that cities will keep growing, especially since job opportunities remain concentrated there, so migration from rural areas is unlikely to slow soon.

cues.cue: housing shortages / worsen / in major cities
models: It is almost certain that housing shortages will worsen in major cities, and the evidence for this is the steady rise in urban population figures each year.

cues.cue: some young people / return / to smaller towns eventually
models: There is every likelihood that some young people will return to smaller towns eventually, and this is supported by growing interest in remote work and lower living costs.

cues.cue: urban populations / continue / to expand steadily
models: It is highly likely that urban populations will continue to expand steadily, given that career prospects remain stronger in cities, and this strongly suggests the trend will persist.

cues.cue: smaller cities / attract / more newcomers over time
models: It is reasonable to expect that smaller cities will attract more newcomers over time, given the fact that major cities are becoming increasingly overcrowded, and therefore migration patterns may shift.

cues.cue: rural populations / shrink / further in coming years
models: The odds are that rural populations will shrink further in coming years, which would explain ongoing concerns about ageing communities, and so policymakers may need to respond.

tasks.question: How likely is it that social media will become even more popular?

cues.cue: social media / grow / further
models: There is every likelihood that social media will grow further, and this is supported by the constant rise in new platforms and daily active users.

cues.cue: usage / increase / among older generations too
models: More likely than not, usage will increase among older generations too, which points to platforms designing features aimed at wider age groups, and as a result the user base will diversify.

cues.cue: new platforms / emerge / to compete for attention
models: It is highly likely that new platforms will emerge to compete for attention, given that the market keeps rewarding innovation, and this strongly suggests fierce competition will continue.

cues.cue: screen time / rise / even further
models: In all probability, screen time will rise even further, which means that concerns about digital wellbeing will grow, and therefore regulation may follow.

cues.cue: regulation / limit / some aspects of social media use
models: It seems probable that regulation will limit some aspects of social media use, judging by growing political pressure, and this implies platforms will face stricter rules.

cues.cue: advertising revenue / continue / to climb steadily
models: One can safely predict that advertising revenue will continue to climb steadily, since the trend clearly shows platforms becoming ever more central to marketing budgets.

tasks.question: How likely is it that we will all speak English one day?

cues.cue: English / remain / global
models: It is reasonable to expect that English will remain the global language, given the fact that it already dominates business and education, and therefore its position looks secure.

cues.cue: translation technology / reduce / the need to learn languages
models: It is highly likely that translation technology will reduce the need to learn languages, given how rapidly the tools are improving, and this strongly suggests fewer people will feel pressured to study English.

cues.cue: English / lose / some ground to other major languages
models: The odds are that English will lose some ground to other major languages, which would explain growing interest in Mandarin and Spanish, and so multilingualism may increase.

cues.cue: universal fluency / remain / unlikely for everyone
models: More likely than not, universal fluency will remain unlikely for everyone, which points to persistent gaps in access to education, and as a result full global adoption seems unrealistic.

cues.cue: younger generations / grow up / more multilingual overall
models: It seems probable that younger generations will grow up more multilingual overall, judging by current trends in early language education, and this implies English will be one language among several.

cues.cue: business communication / rely / heavily on English for decades
models: In all probability, business communication will rely heavily on English for decades, which means the language's dominance is unlikely to fade soon, and therefore learning it will stay valuable.
